correctness.rationale: The published polygonal characterization reduces a homothetic illumination body to an admissible \((k,l)\)-extension with \(k+l=2q\) and \(2q+1<m/2\). For equally spaced outward normals, direct intersection of the two prescribed sidelines yields \(A h_{i-q-1}+B h_{i+q}=\mu D h_i\), where \(A=\sin(q\phi)\), \(B=\sin((q+1)\phi)\), and \(D=\sin((2q+1)\phi)\) are positive. Summing gives \(\mu D=A+B\). A nonconstant Fourier mode would therefore require \(A z^{-(q+1)}+Bz^q=A+B\); equality in the triangle inequality forces both unit factors to be one, and coprimality of \(q,q+1\) forces \(z=1\). Thus all supports are equal and the polygon is regular. The actual frozen verifier was read and stress-tests the Fourier obstruction and sideline intersections.
correctness.risk: The result depends essentially on equal angular spacing and does not settle non-equiangular polygons.
